span: In exceptional cases, to prevent abuse of the process of the Court, the High Court might in exercise of its inherent powers under Section 482 quash criminal proceedings.
why: Headnote holding: power to quash exists and is wide (even for non-compoundable offences on compromise) but is for exceptional cases, with limits for heinous offences.

span: The High Court should have exercised its inherent power under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.
why: Headnote holding: the criminal proceedings were a counterblast and should have been quashed under s.482.

span: The High Court was not justified in quashing the criminal proceedings in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction.
why: Headnote holding: quashing of cheating proceedings under s.482 is set aside because the complaint discloses the offence.

span: the High Court ought to have exercised the powers under Article 226 of the Constitution of India/482 Cr.P.C. and ought to have quashed the impugned FIR
why: Headnote holding: an FIR that is an abuse of process should have been quashed under s.482/Art. 226.

span: Impugned order set aside – FIR and all further proceedings based thereon, quashed.
why: Headnote holding: the High Court ought to have exercised s.482 to quash the FIR; the Supreme Court quashes it.

span: exercise of powers under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. is the exception and not the rule
why: Headnote states the power is the exception, not the rule, yet the FIR is quashed in the case.
